multiScaleR: estimate scales of effect for spatial covariates

Source: R/multiScaleR-package.R
multiScaleR-package.Rd

The scale of effect is the distance over which a landscape variable influences an ecological response, such as how far from a pond the surrounding forest still affects salamander counts. multiScaleR estimates it directly. It weights the raster cells around each survey point with a distance kernel, and it chooses the kernel scale (sigma) that maximizes the likelihood of your regression model. You fit your model once at starting values, and multiScaleR does the search, reports each scale with its uncertainty, and helps you compare, check, and map the result.

Details

Start here

Work through vignette("v01-quickstart", package = "multiScaleR"), then vignette("v02-user-guide", package = "multiScaleR"). Run browseVignettes("multiScaleR") to see all 15 vignettes, which cover mapping, landscape and surface metrics, year-specific rasters, fitting methods, cross-validation, intervals, step selection, spatial fields, distance-removal models, and Bayesian models. multiScaleR-glossary defines the terms they use.

The basic workflow

StepFunctions
1. Describe the covariateskernel_var(), landscape_var(), surface_var(), msr_vars()
2. Prepare the points and rasterskernel_prep(), kernel_prep_by_group(), estimate_multiscale_ram()
3. Fit your model at starting valuesYour usual function, such as glm() or unmarked::pcount()
4. Estimate the scalesmultiScale_optim() or multiScale_bayes()
5. Read and check the fitsummary(), plot(), diagnostics(), profile_sigma(), kernel_dist(), plot_kernel()
6. Compare modelsaic_tab(), bic_tab(), cross_validate(), cv_tab(), select_cv()
7. Predict and mappredict(), kernel_scale.raster(), plot_marginal_effects(), prepare_prediction()

Specialized models and tools

  • Choosing a fitting method: multiScaleR-fitting-methods describes each backend of multiScale_optim().

  • Cross-validation for other model types: cross_validate_glm(), cross_validate_clogit(), cross_validate_field(), cross_validate_mixed(), cross_validate_bayes(), with fold builders spatial_cv_folds() and grouped_cv_folds().

  • Occupancy and abundance models from unmarked: prepare_unmarked_data(), validate_unmarked_data().

  • Distance-removal models: prepare_gdr_histories(), prepare_gdr_intervals(), expand_gdr_intervals(), gdr_start_values(), make_gdr_refitter(), fit_gdr_response_field(), response_field_geometry().

  • Bayesian models, in which a scale may vary among years or with a covariate: multiScale_bayes(), check_bayes_setup(), simulate_bayes_prior(), posterior_scales(), predict_scales(), diagnose_bayes_scales(), diagnose_bayes_probabilities(), diagnose_bayes_laplace().

  • Assessing NB2 scales over the full likelihood range: scale_inference().

  • Simulating data with known scales of effect: sim_rast(), sim_dat(), sim_dat_unmarked(), sim_dat_gdr().

Experimental tools

These tools are experimental. Their arguments and results may change in a later release without a deprecation period: cross_validate_bayes(), cross_validate_mixed(), the count, binary, and positive families of cross_validate_field(), diagnose_bayes_laplace(), and the radius_grid argument of multiScale_optim().

Examples

# Estimate the scale of effect of habitat on simulated counts
data(pts)
data(count_data)
hab <- terra::rast(system.file("extdata", "hab.tif",
                               package = "multiScaleR"))
inputs <- kernel_prep(pts = pts, raster_stack = hab, max_D = 250,
                      kernel = "gaussian", verbose = FALSE)
start_model <- glm(y ~ hab, family = poisson, data = count_data)
fit <- multiScale_optim(start_model, inputs, verbose = FALSE)
summary(fit)   # sigma near the simulated value of 75 map units
